bg.comment: Surface + border, the same separation Popover uses, rather than the inverted chip many systems reach for. An inverted tooltip would need `color.bg.inverse` and `color.fg.inverse` in TIER 2 - public API, permanent at publish - and neither exists. Adding a public pair to style one component is the wrong order of decision: if Clara wants an inverse surface it should arrive as its own decision, serving more than a tooltip.

padding-inline.comment: The control padding pair rather than space.stack: a tooltip is a chip the size of a control, not a stacked panel, and these are the only tier 2 spaces that scale with density.

max-inline-size.comment: A raw dimension, following popover.max-inline-size and modal.width-*. A tooltip width has no semantic ancestor in tier 2 size, and inventing one would put a tooltip-shaped value in the public layer. Narrower than a popover's 20rem: a tooltip carries a sentence, not a panel.

font-size.comment: A tooltip PORTALS to document.body, so it does not even inherit from where its trigger lives - with no declaration its size is the consumer's body font, not Clara's scale. Measured at 13px on a page whose body font-size was 13px, against font.body = 14px, which is below the legibility floor D0104 sets for text that carries meaning. This string is the description of a control (it is what aria-describedby points at), so D0104's implementer test answers yes on the first question and stops there. Precedent: .clara-modal__description pins font.body for the same reason. NOTE: no braces in this comment - Style Dictionary resolves brace expressions as token references wherever they appear, so a CSS snippet written inline here becomes a reference to a token that does not exist, and the build fails with an error naming neither the file nor the text.
